text:
marta: FYI, customer reports streaming responses from Node SDK (edge runtime) stall after an auth token rotation. intermittent, but reproducible in their Vercel edge deployment.

support-bot: New escalation created: INC-2026-2543 (linked). Customer: fintech-app-prod. Severity: high (latency + user-visible hangs).

alex: Can you paste a minimal repro? Is it ReadableStream.getReader() hanging or just no data after a 401?

marta: They say sequence: 1) long-running SSE stream open; 2) token rotated by upstream auth (401 on next event), SDK retries under the hood; 3) stream never emits 'error' nor 'close' — app-level read blocks. Happens only on Edge runtime (Vercel), not Node server.

sam: Any SDK version info?

marta: Using @redwood/inference-js 1.4.0 (customer tried 1.3.2 -> 1.4.0), Node 18 on dev, Vercel Edge runtime uses our edge bundle.

chen: Quick ask — can you grab raw event frames when this occurs? If SSE sends a 401 HTTP chunk we should surface it.

marta: They attached logs (snippet):

```
[2026-02-15T10:12:03Z] CONNECT /v1/streams/conv/abc123 200
[2026-02-15T11:00:00Z] AUTH_ROTATE requestId=xb-77
[2026-02-15T11:00:01Z] RECEIVE /v1/streams/conv/abc123 401 chunk
[2026-02-15T11:00:01Z] SDK_RETRY attempt=1
[2026-02-15T11:00:10Z] NO_MORE_EVENTS - reader blocked
```

marta: They tried curl to repro from a simple edge function and got:

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer OLD" https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/conv/abc123
# then auth rotates, server returns a 401 chunk, client hangs
```

alex: Ok. Sounds like our edge bundle doesn't propagate the chunked 401 as a stream error in ReadableStream. On server side we send a status chunk but the edge runtime's fetch streaming semantics differ.

sam: Repro steps requested: minimal function + SDK call + steps to rotate token. Can we ask customer to run this tiny repro in Vercel edge?

marta: Sent them this snippet to run in their edge function (they confirmed):

```
import { createStream } from '@redwood/inference-js/edge';

export default async function handler(req) {
  const res = await createStream({ model: 'gpt-lite', delta: true });
  const reader = res.body.getReader();
  while (true) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    console.log('chunk', new TextDecoder().decode(value));
  }
}
```

marta: They said after token rotation reader.read() never resolves.

chen: Two quick things to try: 1) upgrade to edge bundle 1.4.1 (we rolled a small fix that emits an error event for non-2xx final chunks), 2) if that's not possible, detect 401 frames by inspecting raw chunk and force close the stream.

jordan: For triage: could be a combination of Vercel's web-streams polyfill + our SSE handling. Edge polyfills sometimes swallow the underlying connection close. We should request a raw tcp capture? Might be heavy.

alex: I'll reproduce locally on our Vercel deploy preview. If I can hit the hang I'll open a runtime PR to ensure non-OK frames call controller.error(...) so getReader() rejects.

sam: Short-term customer workaround: pin SDK to 1.4.1-edge-fix (private build) or fallback to polling. Also instruct to detect inactivity with a timer and recreate stream on timeout.

marta: Customer accepted workaround and asked for ETA for patch. Told them we aim to push a patch in 24-48h and provide a private build. They also shared a small repo link: https://github.com/fintech-corp/repro-stream-hang (private).

alex: Thanks. I'll prioritize reproducer + fix. I'll post back when I have a failing deploy & repro.

chen: Note for release notes: mention edge-specific SSE error propagation fix + token-rotation tests in CI.

marta: Adding note: customer also reported billing spikes during repeated reconnect attempts before the hang — we should include mitigation so retries don't hammer tokens.

alex: Good catch. We'll add exponential backoff + cap retry attempts when 401 seen.

marta: I'll keep the ticket updated. :thumbsup:
